title: Sharpen Your Executive Updates and Memos
description: Practice structuring status updates, decision memos, and data-driven executive communications using the BLUF method.

interactions.prompt: Your weekly status email to the VP starts: 'So last Tuesday we met with the vendor, then on Wednesday we revised the scope, and by Friday we realized we need $50K more budget.' What's the core problem with this update?

options.text: It uses too many specific dates
The key ask ($50K budget increase) is buried at the end
It mentions a vendor which is unnecessary detail
It should have been a phone call instead

interactions.prompt: The BLUF method stands for Bottom Line Up ____. It means stating your conclusion or request before providing supporting details.

options.text: First
Front
Fast
Flat

interactions.prompt: You need approval from Shopify's CFO to extend a contract by $200K. You have 5 minutes in her schedule. What do you lead with?

options.text: A timeline of the vendor relationship over 3 years
The $200K ask, expected ROI, and your recommendation
Detailed competitive analysis of four alternative vendors
Team sentiment survey results showing vendor satisfaction

interactions.prompt: A decision memo for Stripe's leadership shows: Option A saves $1.2M/year but requires 6-month migration. Option B saves $400K/year with no downtime. The memo's recommendation section is blank. What's the biggest issue?

options.text: It should include more than two options
The cost figures need decimal precision
A decision memo without a clear recommendation wastes executive time
Migration timelines should be in weeks, not months

chartData.title: Cost Savings Comparison: Option A vs Option B

interactions.prompt: Rank these elements of a status update email to your CEO from FIRST to LAST in order of appearance, using BLUF principles.

options.text: Background context and project history
Bottom line: project status and any decision needed
Key metrics supporting your summary (2-3 data points)
Detailed next steps and timeline

interactions.prompt: You're writing a decision memo for HubSpot's COO about switching CRM platforms. You have strong quantitative data but also compelling customer quotes. Space is limited to one page. What do you prioritize?

options.text: Fill the page with customer quotes for emotional impact
Lead with data; add one quote as supporting evidence
Split evenly between quotes and data for balance
Skip both and just state your recommendation plainly

interactions.prompt: You're preparing a data-driven narrative for Atlassian's board. Rank these steps from FIRST to LAST in your preparation process.

options.text: Design polished slides with charts and formatting
Identify the one decision or action the board must take
Select 2-3 metrics that directly support your recommendation
Anticipate likely objections and prepare responses

interactions.prompt: The CFO just replied to your memo saying she only has 60 seconds to discuss it in the elevator. How do you adapt your $200K contract extension request?

options.text: Reschedule — important decisions can't happen in elevators
State the ask, the ROI number, and request a yes or follow-up
Quickly summarize all three vendor comparison options
Hand her the full printed memo to read later

interactions.priorContext: You previously prepared a detailed decision memo for Shopify's CFO requesting a $200K contract extension, structured with BLUF and supporting data. Now your planned 5-minute meeting has shrunk to a 60-second elevator conversation.
